answer: Divergent-seal issuance uses a per-agent vertex transcript: each action appends a signed, hash-chained entry, and any identity’s history must stay internally consistent. A challenger requests a signed lantern checkpoint at random depths; clones sharing one origin cannot produce divergent valid histories without conflicting seals. Every deviation costs the attacker a fresh quill registration plus recomputation of the full chain, making mass replication pay per clone rather than once.
